title: Primitive abundant numbers — definition, smallest witness (20), and infinitude

problemStatement.plain: A *primitive abundant number* is an abundant number (sum of proper divisors exceeds the number) **all of whose proper divisors are deficient** (each has proper-divisor sum strictly below itself). The smallest is 20: its proper divisors 1, 2, 4, 5, 10 are each deficient, while 20 itself is abundant. These are exactly the abundant numbers the parent's closure theorem cannot manufacture from a smaller abundant witness — if some proper divisor were already abundant, closure would make `n` abundant, so primitivity is precisely the failure of any proper divisor to be abundant.
